items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 22 at 1:50PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
An incoming system will move over the panhandle Sunday into Monday,
bringing extended periods of moderate to heavy rain for the southern
panhandle. Highest rain rates are expected during Sunday evening and
overnight, primarily for Ketchikan, Metlakatla, and Misty Fjords.
Highest uncertainty is the location of heaviest rain, which has a
30% chance to shift east of Ketchikan and Metlakatla. Small streams
and rivers may rise, but no flooding is expected at this time.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 22 at 1:37PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
A Bering Sea low will move into the Gulf of Anadyr Sunday then
into the Chukchi Sea on Monday. South-southwest winds will
increase water levels to around 1 to 3 feet above the normal high
tide line during the Monday and Tuesday high tides in the Seward
Peninsula. Water levels around 2 to 4 feet above the normal high
tide line are possible from Kotzebue to Kivalina. There is still
quite a bit of uncertainty with the exact water level heights and
they will be monitored over the next few days.
items.areas: Kivalina and Red Dog Dock; Baldwin Peninsula; Northern Seward Peninsula; Shishmaref; Bering Strait Coast
